description: Conformance corpus for standards/service.md. 'validity': the value must validate (or fail) against the named $def in health.schema.json, or against logline.schema.json where def is 'logLine'. 'lifecycle': black-box cases a running service must satisfy — the harness drives the described stimulus and asserts 'expect'. An implementation passes the whole file or names the case it fails.

validity.note: the running service says which build it is (SC5)
liveness answers 'is the process alive'; a process answering at all is alive (SC1)
a required dependency down is 503 — but the service is up and saying so, not exiting (SC6)
an optional dependency down is 200 + degraded: the service was built to tolerate this, and 503 here would be a self-inflicted outage (SC1, SC6)
misconfiguration blocks serving, not observability: endpoints up, every broken variable named, no exit and no crashloop (SC3, SC6)
every check declares whether the service can serve without it; defaulting that decision is how an optional dependency becomes an outage (SC1)
one probe worked or did not; degradation is the service's property, derived from which checks failed
reporting ok while checking nothing converts an unknown into a wrong answer (SC1)
a check that passes slowly is the earliest warning of one that will fail (SC1)
outside request context, the context block is absent and that is correct (OC4)
a line carrying any request-scoped id carries the floor pair; 'failed for this tenant, in no identifiable request' is not a lead (OC4)
the timestamp is the identifiers contract's (IP4)

lifecycle.note: the status code is what a load balancer reads; liveness stays 200 because the process is alive and restarting it fixes nothing (SC1)

lifecycle.stimulus: the service is started with no dependency reachable at all
lifecycle.note: the core of SC6: a dependency the service must survive losing at runtime is not a reason to refuse to start. Endpoints up, real state reported, no crashloop.

lifecycle.stimulus: every required dependency reachable, one optional dependency unreachable
lifecycle.note: the mode gracefully-degrading code was written for; refusing to start throws that code away (SC6)

lifecycle.stimulus: a dependency that takes 10s to answer its first probe

GET /healthz.within: the startup budget, not gated on the probe

lifecycle.note: the listener and both endpoints come up as early as the process can bring them up; everything else happens after and concurrently (SC6)

GET /readyz.body.checks[name=configuration].detail: names both missing variables, not the first

lifecycle.note: misconfiguration blocks serving, never observability. Readiness that never passes is how an orchestrator fails a rollout and rolls back, and it beats a crashloop for diagnosis (SC3, SC6)

expect.first_lines: a log line carrying service, version, commit and built_at

lifecycle.note: unconditional, so CI can assert it without depending on how a repository exposes endpoints (SC5)

lifecycle.stimulus: SIGTERM while one request is in flight
lifecycle.note: the order is the rule: readiness first is what makes a rolling deploy non-lossy (SC4)

lifecycle.stimulus: SIGTERM with work still running at the drain deadline
lifecycle.note: work lost quietly is work nobody reconciles (SC4)
